issues: What is the legal test for determining whether an activity constitutes a business (source of income) rather than a hobby or personal expenditure?
What factors do courts consider in applying the profit motive test, including systematic and regular conduct, commercial approach, and expectation of profit?
What is the onus of proof on the taxpayer to establish that an activity is a business?
What is the effect of sustained losses over multiple years on the characterization of an activity as a business?
Are losses from an activity characterized as a hobby deductible under the Income Tax Act?
key_facts: activity operated at a loss for several years
losses were deducted on tax returns
CRA reassessed and recharacterized the activity as a hobby
candidate_statutes: Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.), s. 8
Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.), s. 18
